title: Touring benefits and the call from Hank Leo to teach in Rome, NY
summary: After Katrina he toured benefit shows, stayed at his grandparents' place near Baton Rouge, and Hank Leo invited him to work with the YMCA music program.

venues.name: YMCA Center for the Creative Arts

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: in New Orleans it’s I think mostly the economy is based on tourism. And so yeah, I had to try to find an alternate, some other things to do. I was doing some touring, on the road and everything, and that was mostly when there was a lot of publicity about the hurricane. I mean people obviously were doing what they could to help people from New Orleans in other parts of the country. So there were a lot of musical engagements and performances to help raise money and funds for victims of Hurricane Katrina. And so I did a lot of that touring right after thing — and when it got down in the media so did those gigs, so I was kind of just staying — I went back up and had a place a little north, northwest of Baton Rogue, it was in the country, it was my grandparents’ place, and I was staying there. That’s when my friend Hank Leo called me up and asked me what was going on with me and if I’d be interested in coming up and working with the Y, with the music program with the kids here.
